value.body: A maintenance engineer keeps machines, utilities and electrical systems in a plant running. Manufacturers, process plants, power stations and large facilities hire them. A typical day mixes planned checks, fixing breakdowns, logging work and coordinating with production so stoppages stay short.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / Diploma in Mechanical or Electrical

items.label: Common tools
items.value: CMMS / SAP PM, multimeters, vibration and thermal tools

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Shift duty and on-call for breakdowns is common

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as a graduate engineer trainee (GET) or junior engineer at a plant, through campus placement or direct application. Diploma holders often enter as technicians and move up with experience.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Safety practices such as lockout–tagout and permits to work
Keeping maintenance logs and spare-parts records

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is plant-based, often in industrial areas away from big cities.
Common next roles: maintenance in-charge, reliability engineer, plant engineering manager.
Electrical maintenance roles may need a state electrical supervisor licence for some work.
